notes.title: Check the outer seal
notes.body: Read the seal number against the paper manifest before moving the crate. If the security strip is torn, keep the crate in its present freezer and contact the receiving technician for a replacement transfer record.

notes.title: Prepare the receiving shelf
notes.body: Clear the assigned shelf and place the receiving tray within easy reach. Keep unrelated specimens in their labeled compartments so that the new crate can be set down without moving other active research material.

notes.title: Keep the lid closed
notes.body: Carry the crate with its insulated lid firmly latched. Open it only inside the receiving cold room, after the technician confirms the destination label and has the temperature logger ready for the arrival reading.

notes.title: Use the protected route
notes.body: Take the marked indoor corridor between the loading room and the cold store. Avoid leaving the crate beside an exterior doorway while waiting for a lift; ask a colleague to hold the internal door instead.

notes.title: Record the logger reading
notes.body: At the receiving shelf, read the logger without removing its probe from the packing sleeve. Write the displayed value and the time on the manifest, then return the logger to its original position inside the crate.

notes.title: Separate a suspect container
notes.body: If one container has a loose cap or a damaged label, keep that container in the secondary tray. Do not relabel it from memory. Record its position and ask the receiving technician to confirm the sample identity.

notes.title: Confirm the handoff
notes.body: Give the receiving technician the manifest and wait for a verbal acknowledgement of the crate identifier. The app records a release request only; the receiving team still completes its normal physical inventory and handoff procedure.

notes.title: Store the paperwork
notes.body: Leave the signed manifest in the cold-room document sleeve after the handoff is complete. Keep the crate identifier visible at the front of the shelf so the next shift can find both the specimens and their record.

initial.title: Evening transfer for the coastal laboratory

notes.title: Check the coastal manifest
notes.body: Match the seal number to the coastal manifest before moving the crate. Keep a damaged seal in the current freezer and call the receiving technician.

notes.title: Prepare the shelf
notes.body: Clear the coastal receiving shelf and put its tray within reach. Leave other specimens in their labeled compartments while the new crate is being placed.

notes.title: Keep the lid closed
notes.body: Carry the crate with its insulated lid latched. Open it inside the receiving cold room after the technician checks the destination and prepares the logger.

notes.title: Follow the indoor route
notes.body: Use the marked indoor corridor. Ask a colleague to hold the internal door so the crate does not wait beside an exterior entrance.

notes.title: Read the logger
notes.body: Read the logger with its probe still in the packing sleeve. Record the displayed temperature and arrival time on the manifest before replacing the lid.

notes.title: Separate suspect containers
notes.body: Put a container with a loose cap or damaged label in the secondary tray. Ask the technician to verify its identity before writing a replacement label.

notes.title: Confirm the handoff
notes.body: Wait for the technician to acknowledge the crate identifier. This app records the release request; the receiving team completes its separate physical inventory and signature.

notes.title: Leave the paperwork
notes.body: Place the signed manifest in the cold-room sleeve. Keep the crate identifier facing the aisle so the next shift can find the specimens and their record.

title-wrapping.value: The title displays every supplied word through natural wrapping, without truncation or an ellipsis.

body-wrapping.value: Every expanded body paragraph displays its complete supplied text through natural wrapping without an ellipsis.

title-hierarchy.value: The title is visually more prominent than the expanded section headings.

horizontal-clipping.value: All visible text and controls remain inside the component horizontal bounds without clipping.

row-overlap.value: Successive rows in the component do not visually overlap.

flow-order.value: Main component blocks occur in one vertical column in this order: ink accent, title, subtitle, status, disclosure, any expanded sections, choice, primary.

collapsed-content.value: The handling notes body paragraphs are hidden while the disclosure is closed.

expanded-order.value: The eight expanded handling notes heading/body pairs appear in caller order.

obligations.clause: The current caller title is exposed with its complete exact text.
The current caller summary uses the specified exact string composition.
The status follows the independently specified guard/state precedence.
Disclosure wording reflects the current open or closed local state.
The native choice has its exact specified accessible label.
The native selected trait reflects the local acknowledgement or Wi-Fi preference.
The native choice becomes disabled after the request and resets on replacement.
The primary uses the exact normal or requested label.
The primary native enabled state follows the business gates and request state.
The primary actual native control boundary is 56 pt/dp high within independently fixed 0.75 pt/dp tolerance.
The primary native control top edge is 12 pt/dp below the choice native control bottom edge, within independently fixed 0.75 pt/dp tolerance.
The status band leading inset has the independently fixed opaque state-role fill.
The primary leading inset has the independently fixed enabled/disabled fill.
The surface gutter renders the independently fixed opaque white surface role.
The component canvas gutter renders the independently fixed opaque canvas role.
The solid ink accent renders the independently fixed opaque navy ink role.
